Whether the expiration a read-back carries is reached on the day of a round

mail_expiration_reached.Rd

The stored expiration is the day after the last day of access, so it is reached when it is not later than the day of the round: REDCap denies access when expiration <= TODAY, and its TODAY is the date in Rome, redcap_today(). The day is the one in Rome of the instant at, not the clock of whoever composes the message, so the same row says the same thing whenever it is read and the tests do not depend on the machine. The round takes the date it hands to validate_request(), the choice of lapsed and the gate from the same instant, at, so between 22:00 and 24:00 UTC, when the date in Rome is already the next day, the message and the gate agree with REDCap. A round whose day in Rome turns before it writes to an instance acts on nothing there. One whose day turns after the write, while its messages leave, still tells them on the day of at, the day the access was granted.

Usage

mail_expiration_reached(applied_as, at)

Arguments

applied_as

The row's read-back, role_name=...; dag_name=...; expiration=....

at

The time of the round, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M" in UTC. A bare date is read as the day itself.

Value

TRUE when both carry a date and the expiration is not later than the day of at; FALSE otherwise, which is the answer for every row that says nothing readable.
